title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the 17th Batch of Guiding Cases
ruling_gist_en:
1. Administrative licenses have statutory time limits. When granting an administrative license, the administrative authority shall clearly inform the administrative counterpart of the time limit of the license, and the administrative counterpart also has the right to know the time limit.

2. If the administrative counterpart claims that the administrative license has no time limit merely on the ground that the administrative authority did not inform the time limit, the people's court shall not support such claim.

3. If the administrative authority, when granting the administrative license, fails to inform the time limit, and later terminates the administrative counterpart's rights under the license on the ground that the time limit has expired, such act constitutes a violation of administrative procedures. The people's court shall, in accordance with law, render a judgment to quash the challenged administrative act. However, if quashing the challenged administrative act would cause obvious adverse effects on public interests and the order of administrative management, the people's court shall render a judgment to confirm the illegality of the challenged administrative act.
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the 17th Batch of Guiding Cases

Fa [2017] No. 332

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Upon discussion and approval by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, the five cases of Zhang Daowen, Tao Ren, et al. v. People's Government of Jianyang City, Sichuan Province — dispute over infringement of the right to operate passenger human-powered tricycles (Guiding Cases Nos. 88-92), are hereby issued as the 17th batch of guiding cases for reference in adjudicating similar cases.

November 15, 2017

Guiding Case No. 88

Zhang Daowen, Tao Ren, et al. v. People's Government of Jianyang City, Sichuan Province — dispute over infringement of the right to operate passenger human-powered tricycles

(Discussed and approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on November 15, 2017)

Keywords: administrative / administrative license / time limit / obligation of notification / administrative procedure / judgment confirming illegality

Ruling Gist

1. An administrative license has a statutory time limit. When granting an administrative license, the administrative organ shall clearly inform the party of the time limit of the administrative license, and the party also has the right to know the time limit of the administrative license.

2. Where a party merely claims that the administrative license has no time limit on the ground that the administrative organ failed to inform the party of the time limit, the People's Court shall not support such claim.

3. Where an administrative organ fails to inform the party of the time limit when granting the administrative license, and later terminates the party's rights under the administrative license on the ground that the time limit has expired, this constitutes an illegality in the administrative procedure. The People's Court shall, in accordance with the law, render a judgment to annul the sued administrative act. However, if annulling the sued administrative act would cause obvious adverse effects on public interest and the administrative management order, the People's Court shall render a judgment to confirm the illegality of the sued administrative act.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 89, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

On December 12, 1994, the People's Government of Jianyang City, Sichuan Province (hereinafter "Jianyang City Government") issued a notice to implement quota management for passenger human-powered tricycles within the urban area. In August 1996, the Jianyang City Government collected a fee of RMB 3,500 per person for the paid use of the right to operate reconstruction of elderly passenger human-powered vehicles into passenger human-powered tricycles (240 tricycles). In November 1996, the Jianyang City Government collected a fee of RMB 2,000 per person for the paid use of the right to operate the existing 161 passenger human-powered tricycles. Starting from November 1996, the Jianyang City Government began implementing paid use of operating rights, and relevant authorities also collected related fees for the quota of 401 passenger human-powered tricycles. On July 15 and July 28, 1999, the Jianyang City Government issued the "Notice on Regulating the Order of Small Vehicle Operations in the Urban Area" (hereinafter "Notice") and the "Supplementary Notice on Regulating the Order of Small Vehicle Operations in the Urban Area" (hereinafter "Supplementary Notice") concerning passenger human-powered tricycles whose paid use period had expired for two years. Among them, the "Notice" required that "operators of passenger human-powered tricycles who originally held valid licenses must re-register at the Municipal Traffic Police Brigade Office from July 19 to July 20, 1999." The "Supplementary Notice" required that "upon review, registered operators who obtain the operating right shall pay a fee for the paid use of the operating right at the standard of RMB 8,000 per tricycle (at the standard of RMB 7,200 per tricycle for those meeting the conditions of Article 6 of the 'Notice')." Zhang Daowen, Tao Ren, and other 182 operators of passenger human-powered tricycles believed that the provisions of Article 6 of the "Notice" and Article 2 of the "Supplementary Notice" issued by the Jianyang City Government constituted duplicate fees and infringed upon their lawful operating rights. They filed an administrative lawsuit with the People's Court of Jianyang City, Sichuan Province, requesting a judgment to annul the aforementioned "Notice" and "Supplementary Notice" issued by the Jianyang City Government.

Judgment

On November 9, 1999, the People's Court of Jianyang City, Sichuan Province, rendered a judgment under (1999) Jianyang Xing Chu Zi No. 36, in accordance with Article 54, Item 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, upholding the administrative acts of the Municipal Government on July 15, 1999, and July 28, 1999. Zhang Daowen, Tao Ren, et al. appealed. On March 2, 2000, the Intermediate People's Court of Ziyang Prefecture, Sichuan Province, rendered an administrative judgment under (2000) Zi Xing Zhong Zi No. 6, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. On June 13, 2001, the High People's Court of Sichuan Province issued an administrative ruling under (2001) Chuan Xing Jian Zi No. 1, directing the Intermediate People's Court of Ziyang City (formerly Ziyang Prefecture) to conduct a retrial. On November 3, 2001, the Intermediate People's Court of Ziyang City, Sichuan Province, rendered a judgment under (2001) Zi Xing Zai Zhong Zi No. 1, annulling the original first-instance and second-instance judgments and dismissing the claims of the original plaintiffs. Zhang Daowen, Tao Ren, et al. appealed, and filed a complaint with the High People's Court of Sichuan Province. On July 11, 2002, the High People's Court of Sichuan Province issued a Notice of Rejection of Retrial Application under (2002) Chuan Xing Jian Zi No. 4. Zhang Daowen, Tao Ren, et al. appealed, and applied to the Supreme People's Court for a retrial. On March 23, 2016, the Supreme People's Court ruled to bring the case up for trial. On May 3, 2017, the Supreme People's Court rendered an administrative judgment under (2016) Zui Gao Fa Xing Zai No. 81: 1. Annulling the judgment under (2001) Zi Xing Zai Zhong Zi No. 1 of the Intermediate People's Court of Ziyang City, Sichuan Province; 2. Confirming the illegality of the "Notice on Regulating the Order of Small Vehicle Operations in the Urban Area" and the "Supplementary Notice on Regulating the Order of Small Vehicle Operations in the Urban Area" issued by the People's Government of Jianyang City, Sichuan Province.

Reasoning

The Supreme People's Court held that this case involved the following three main issues:

Regarding the legality of the sued administrative acts. From the perspective of legal application, Article 4 of the "Regulations of Sichuan Province on Road Transport Management" provides that "transportation administrative departments at all levels are responsible for the adjustment of types and the placement of quantities of for-hire vehicles within their respective administrative regions." Article 24 provides that "with the approval of the People's Government at or above the county level, passenger transport operating rights may be subject to paid use." Article 8 of the "Provisions of Sichuan Province on the Administration of Small Vehicle Passenger Transport" (Chuan Jiao Yun [1994] No. 359) formulated by the Transportation Department of Sichuan Province provides that "when transportation management departments of cities, prefectures, or districts implement quota management for small passenger vehicles, with the approval of the local government, the method of paid use of operation permits may be adopted, but the period of paid use shall not exceed two years at a time." It can be seen that the local regulations of Sichuan Province have clearly stipulated that passenger transport operating rights may be subject to paid use. Although the normative document formulated by the Transportation Department of Sichuan Province predates the local regulations, the provision in that normative document for a limited period of paid use of operation permits does not conflict with the local regulations. Based on the needs of administrative law enforcement and administrative management, passenger transport operating rights also need to be set with a certain time limit. From the perspective of the administrative procedure of the sued acts, the procedure was clearly improper. The content of the sued administrative acts was the measure of re-registering operators of passenger human-powered tricycles who originally held valid licenses, requiring those who passed the review to pay a fee for paid use, and treating those who failed to register within the time limit as automatically abandoning their rights. The sued acts imposed a fee for paid use on operators of passenger human-powered tricycles who had already obtained valid licenses, and the rights of those operators were obtained through operating right licensing in 1996. There was a successive and connecting relationship between the two administrative acts. For the 1996 licensing act, when the administrative organ granted an administrative license or other beneficial administrative acts, it should have clearly informed the party of the time limit of the administrative license. When the administrative organ grants an administrative license, the party also has the right to know the time limit of the administrative license. When the administrative organ implemented the licensing of passenger human-powered tricycle operating rights in 1996, it failed to inform Zhang Daowen, Tao Ren, et al. of the two-year period of paid use of the operating rights. Zhang Daowen, Tao Ren, et al. were unaware of the period of paid use of their operating rights. The 1996 licensing act of the Jianyang City Government had obvious procedural impropriety, which directly led to the procedural impropriety of the sued administrative acts in this case, which had a successive relationship with the former.

Regarding the time limit of the operating rights of passenger human-powered tricycles. The applicants argued that because the Jianyang City Government failed to inform them of the time limit when implementing the licensing of passenger human-powered tricycle operating rights in 1996, they believed that the operating license had no time limit. The Supreme People's Court held that the purpose of the Jianyang City Government in implementing the licensing of passenger human-powered tricycle operating rights was to regulate the order of passenger human-powered tricycle operations. Passenger human-powered tricycles are a method of public resource allocation involving public interest, and setting a certain time limit is necessary. Objectively, the "Provisions of Sichuan Province on the Administration of Small Vehicle Passenger Transport" (Chuan Jiao Yun [1994] No. 359) formulated by the Transportation Department of Sichuan Province also clarified the time limit of the license. The Jianyang City Government failed to inform the applicants of the time limit of the license, which constituted a procedural defect. However, the Supreme People's Court did not support the applicants' claim that the administrative license had no time limit merely on that ground.

Regarding the issue of Zhang Daowen, Tao Ren, et al. actually enjoying the "benefit to the people" policies. The Jianyang City Government carried out rectification based on the actual local problems such as serious overload of roads, severe air and noise pollution, "dirty, chaotic, and poor" conditions, and "crowded, blocked, and narrow" conditions, which met the needs of urban management and the wishes of the people, and its legitimacy should be affirmed. To resolve the petition issues left over from this lawsuit, the Jianyang City Government successively implemented two "benefit to the people" actions, making positive efforts to substantially resolve the disputes in this case, and its subsequent actions should also be affirmed. This Court confirms the fact that Zhang Daowen, Tao Ren, et al. accepted the capacity allocation plan for exiting the market operation and made commitments. However, when administrative organs take administrative actions, they must adhere to the principle of administration according to law and ensure that administrative powers are exercised in accordance with statutory procedures.

The Supreme People's Court held that there were procedural defects in the "Notice" and "Supplementary Notice" issued by the Jianyang City Government, which constituted obvious impropriety. However, considering that after the sued administrative acts were made, the traffic order in the urban area of Jianyang City improved, the road capacity of the city increased, the urban appearance continued to improve, and through the two "benefit to the people" actions, the vast majority of the original 401 tricycles had been replaced in batches, if the sued administrative acts were to be annulled, it would cause obvious adverse effects on the administrative management order and public interest. The Supreme People's Court, in accordance with the provisions of Article 58 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" concerning situation judgments, confirmed the illegality of the sued administrative acts.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Liang Fengyun, Wang Haifeng, Tong Lei)

Guiding Case No. 89

"Bei Yan Yun Yi" v. Yanshan Police Station of Lixia Branch of Jinan Public Security Bureau — dispute over public security administrative registration

(Discussed and approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on November 15, 2017)

Keywords: administrative / public security administrative registration / right to name / public order and good customs / legitimate reason

Ruling Gist

The selection or creation of a surname by a citizen shall conform to traditional Chinese culture and ethical concepts. Selecting a surname other than the father's surname or the mother's surname, or creating a new surname, based solely on personal preference and desire, does not fall within the scope of "other legitimate reasons that do not violate public order and good customs" as provided in Paragraph 2, Item 3 of the Interpretation of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Article 99, Paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 22 of the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 99, Paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China

Article 22 of the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China

Interpretation of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Article 99, Paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 22 of the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

Lü Xiaofeng, the legal representative of the plaintiff "Bei Yan Yun Yi," alleged that his wife, Zhang Ruizheng, gave birth to a daughter in the hospital, named her "Bei Yan Yun Yi," and obtained the birth certificate and the newborn registration record for household registration in the family planning service handbook. When applying for household registration for the daughter, the defendant, Yanshan Police Station of Lixia Branch of Jinan Public Security Bureau (hereinafter "Yanshan Police Station"), refused to register the household registration. The reason given was that the child's surname must follow either the father's surname or the mother's surname, i.e., the surname "Lü" or "Zhang." Pursuant to the provisions of the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Marriage Law") and the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "General Principles of Civil Law") concerning the right to name, the plaintiff requested the court to find that the defendant's act of refusing to register the household registration under the name "Bei Yan Yun Yi" was illegal.

The defendant, Yanshan Police Station, argued that it was correct to refuse the household registration under the name "Bei Yan Yun Yi" in accordance with the law and superior documents. The General Principles of Civil Law stipulate that citizens enjoy the right to a name, but there are no specific provisions. In a press conference held by the Supreme People's Court on December 23, 2009, regarding the issue of changing the surname of a child after divorce, it was stated that Article 22 of the Marriage Law is a specific provision of Chinese law on the issue of children's surnames. That article provides that a child may take either the father's surname or the mother's surname, but does not provide for taking a third surname. Administrative organs must act in accordance with the law; actions not clearly authorized by law cannot be implemented. Neither the plaintiff nor the administrative organs have the right to make an expansive interpretation of the law. This means that a child only has two options: to take the father's surname or the mother's surname. From another perspective, the purpose of the law in recognizing the right to a name is to enable citizens to be clearly distinguished from others by a written symbol, i.e., a name, thereby realizing their personality and rights. The right to a name, like other rights, is subject to legal restrictions and cannot be abused. A newborn taking the father's surname or the mother's surname is a traditional Chinese custom. This custom signifies blood relations. Taking the father's surname or the mother's surname indicates a blood relationship, which can to a large extent prevent consanguineous marriage. However, taking a third surname contradicts this traditional custom and the original meaning of a surname. Public security organs across the country, in implementing Article 22 of the Marriage Law concerning the issue of children's surnames, have a uniform standard: a child shall take the father's surname or the mother's surname. In summary, the act of refusing the plaintiff's legal representative's application for household registration using the name "Bei Yan Yun Yi" was correct. The defendant respectfully requests the People's Court to dismiss the plaintiff's claims in accordance with the law.

The court found through trial that the plaintiff "Bei Yan Yun Yi" was born on January 25, 2009. Her father's name is Lü Xiaofeng, and her mother's name is Zhang Ruizheng. Due to their passion for poetry, songs, and traditional Chinese culture, the couple Lü Xiaofeng and Zhang Ruizheng decided to name their beloved daughter "Bei Yan Yun Yi" and obtained the newborn birth certificate and the newborn registration record for household registration in the family planning service handbook under the name "Bei Yan Yun Yi." In February 2009, Lü Xiaofeng went to Yanshan Police Station to apply for household registration for his daughter. He was informed by the police officer that the surname of the person to be registered must follow the father's surname or the mother's surname, i.e., "Lü" or "Zhang"; otherwise, the conditions for household registration would not be met. Because Lü Xiaofeng insisted on applying for household registration for his daughter under the name "Bei Yan Yun Yi," the defendant Yanshan Police Station, in accordance with Article 22 of the Marriage Law, made the specific administrative act of refusing to process the household registration on the same day.

After two public hearings, Lü Xiaofeng, the legal representative of the plaintiff "Bei Yan Yun Yi," stated in court that the name "Bei Yan Yun Yi" he chose for his daughter had "Bei Yan" as the surname and "Yun Yi" as the given name.

Because the case involved issues of legal application that required interpretation or confirmation by the competent authority, the case was suspended for trial by a ruling on March 11, 2010. After the grounds for suspension were eliminated, the case resumed trial on April 21, 2015.

Judgment

The People's Court of Lixia District, Jinan City, rendered an administrative judgment on April 25, 2015, under (2010) Li Xing Chu Zi No. 4: dismissing the plaintiff "Bei Yan Yun Yi's" claim for a declaration that the defendant Yanshan Police Station's act of refusing to register the household registration under the name "Bei Yan Yun Yi" was illegal.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced and served, neither the plaintiff nor the defendant appealed. This judgment has become legally effective.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that on November 1, 2014, the 11th Session of the Standing Committee of the 12th National People's Congress adopted the Interpretation of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Article 99, Paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 22 of the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China. This legislative interpretation provides: "Citizens enjoy the right to a name in accordance with the law. When exercising the right to a name, citizens shall also respect social ethics and shall not harm the public interest. In principle, a citizen shall take the father's surname or the mother's surname. Under any of the following circumstances, a surname other than the father's surname or the mother's surname may be selected: (1) selecting the surname of another direct lineal elder relative by blood; (2) selecting the surname of the person raising the citizen because the citizen is raised by someone other than the statutory supporter; (3) having other legitimate reasons that do not violate public order and good customs. Citizens of ethnic minorities may choose their surnames in accordance with their own ethnic cultural traditions and customs."

In this case, there is no situation of selecting the surname of another lineal elder blood relative or selecting the surname of a person who is not the statutory supporter. The focus of the case is whether the reason put forward by the plaintiff's legal representative, Lü Xiaofeng, meets the condition of "other legitimate reasons that do not violate public order and good customs" under Article 2, Paragraph 3 of the above legislative interpretation. First, from the perspective of social management and development, a child's adoption of a parent's surname facilitates the efficiency of social management, enabling administrative authorities and other members of society to make preliminary judgments about the principal social relationships of the surname user. If random selection or even arbitrary creation of surnames were permitted, it would increase social management costs, be detrimental to society and others, undermine the maintenance of social order and the realization of effective social control, and would likely lead to chaos in social management, increasing the risk and uncertainty of social governance. Second, a citizen's selection of a surname involves public order and good customs. In traditional Chinese culture, the "surname" (xing) in a "name" (xingming) primarily derives from objective inheritance, passed down from ancestors, carrying respect for ancestors and love for the family, reflecting blood lineage, ethical order, and cultural tradition. In contrast, the "given name" (ming) originates from subjective creation, bestowed by parents, carrying personal preferences, personality traits, and parental wishes. Citizens' emphasis on and respect for the inheritance of surnames not only reflect blood relationships and kinship but also embody rich cultural traditions, ethical concepts, and humanistic sentiments, conforming to mainstream values and serving as the carrier and mirror of the cohesion and unity of the Chinese nation. The principle that a child takes the father's or mother's surname conforms to traditional Chinese culture and ethical concepts, and aligns with the will and actual practice of the vast majority of citizens. Conversely, if citizens were allowed to arbitrarily select surnames or even create surnames based solely on personal preferences and wishes, it would impact cultural traditions and ethical concepts, violating social good customs and general moral requirements. Third, citizens lawfully enjoy the right to a name. The exercise of the right to a name is a civil activity and must comply not only with Article 99, Paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law and Article 22 of the Marriage Law, but also with Article 7 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, i.e., it must respect social morality and not harm public interests. Under normal circumstances, the act of selecting a surname other than the father's or mother's surname mainly occurs in situations such as changes in actual fostering relationships, benefits to the minor's physical and mental health, and protection of personal dignity. In this case, the parents of the plaintiff, "Beiyan Yunyi," created the surname "Beiyan" and selected the name "Beiyan Yunyi" for their daughter when registering her household registration, on the grounds that "the name 'Beiyan Yunyi' is taken from four famous classical Chinese poems, symbolizing the parents' best wishes for their daughter." This reason is based solely on personal preferences and wishes in creating a surname, showing obvious arbitrariness, and does not meet the condition under Article 2, Paragraph 3 of the legislative interpretation, and should not be supported.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Ren Jun, Bai Yang, Qian Xin)

Guiding Case No. 90

Bei Huifeng v. Traffic Police Brigade of Haining City Public Security Bureau — dispute over administrative penalty for road traffic management

(Deliberated and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on November 15, 2017)

Keywords: administrative / administrative penalty / yielding of motor vehicles / crossing pedestrian crosswalk

Ruling Gist

Yielding to pedestrians is a basic requirement of civilized and safe driving. When a motor vehicle driver approaches a pedestrian crosswalk, and encounters a pedestrian crossing or stopping on the crosswalk, the driver shall proactively stop and yield, unless the pedestrian clearly signals the motor vehicle to pass first. Where the traffic management department of the public security organ imposes an administrative penalty on a motor vehicle driver who fails to yield to a pedestrian, the people's court shall support such decision.

Related Legal Provisions

Article 47, Paragraph 1 of the Road Traffic Safety Law of the PRC

Basic Facts

The plaintiff, Bei Huifeng, alleged: When he drove vehicle Zhe F1158J (hereinafter "vehicle in question") approaching a pedestrian crosswalk, the pedestrian had already stopped on the crosswalk, thus it did not fall within the scope of "crossing the pedestrian crosswalk." Moreover, Xishan Road, where the vehicle in question was traveling, is a main road in Haining City, with heavy traffic at the incident location and no traffic lights. If motor vehicles had to stop and yield whenever a pedestrian was on the crosswalk, it would significantly affect traffic efficiency. Therefore, he could pass through the crosswalk directly without stopping and yielding, as long as it ensured safe passage, and thus should not be penalized. The Traffic Police Brigade of Haining City Public Security Bureau (hereinafter "Haining Traffic Police Brigade") issued a summary procedure penalty decision for public security traffic management under number 3304811102542425, which was unlawful. Bei Huifeng requested: Revocation of the administrative penalty decision made by the Haining Traffic Police Brigade.

The defendant, Haining Traffic Police Brigade, argued: The pedestrian had entered the crosswalk before the vehicle in question driven by the plaintiff and was crossing it; the vehicle in question should have stopped and yielded. If the pedestrian had already stopped on the crosswalk, the motor vehicle driver could signal the pedestrian to pass quickly, and only if the pedestrian did not move could the motor vehicle pass; otherwise, it constituted a violation. The administrative penalty imposed on Bei Huifeng had clear facts, sufficient and reliable evidence, correct application of law, and lawful procedures. The brigade requested the court to dismiss Bei Huifeng's claims.

The court found through trial: On January 31, 2015, Bei Huifeng drove the vehicle in question along Xishan Road in Haining City. When encountering a pedestrian crossing the crosswalk, he did not stop to yield. The law enforcement traffic police from the Haining Traffic Police Brigade stopped the vehicle on the spot, verified Bei Huifeng's driver identity, applied summary procedures, orally informed Bei Huifeng of the basic facts of the violation, the proposed administrative penalty, the legal basis, and his rights, and after hearing Bei Huifeng's statements and defenses, produced and served on the spot a summary procedure penalty decision for public security traffic management, fining Bei Huifeng RMB 100 and deducting 3 points. Bei Huifeng disagreed and filed an administrative reconsideration with the Haining City People's Government on February 13, 2015. On March 27, the Haining City People's Government issued an administrative reconsideration decision, upholding the penalty decision made by the Haining Traffic Police Brigade. After receiving the reconsideration decision, Bei Huifeng filed a lawsuit with the Haining City People's Court on April 14, 2015.

Judgment

The Haining City People's Court, Zhejiang Province, rendered administrative judgment (2015) Jia Hai Xing Chu Zi No. 6 on June 11, 2015: Dismissed Bei Huifeng's claims. After the judgment was pronounced, Bei Huifeng disagreed and appealed. The Jiaxing Intermediate People's Court, Zhejiang Province, rendered administrative judgment (2015) Zhe Jia Xing Zhong Zi No. 52 on September 10, 2015: Dismissed the appeal and affirmed the original judgment.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held: First, a pedestrian crosswalk is a passage on the roadway specifically designated for pedestrians to cross, serving as a protective line set by law for pedestrians when crossing the road. At road intersections without traffic lights, pedestrians have the right of way on the crosswalk. As a fast means of transport, motor vehicles operate on roads with high danger and are in a stronger position compared to pedestrians. Therefore, certain restrictions must be imposed on the rights of motor vehicles when driving on roads to protect pedestrians. Second, determining whether a pedestrian is "crossing the crosswalk" should be based on a series of continuous actions of the pedestrian within a specific time period, rather than on a specific action at a specific point in time, especially when that specific action is not freely taken by the pedestrian but compelled by external force. At the time of the incident, the pedestrian stepped onto the crosswalk at a relatively fast pace and approached the central area of the intersection at a relatively fast speed. When seeing the vehicle in question driven by Bei Huifeng heading toward the pedestrian's direction, the pedestrian slowed down to confirm whether the vehicle would stop, but did not stop moving. Only when seeing that the vehicle did not significantly decelerate and showed no trend of stopping did the pedestrian have to stop for safety. If the vehicle had clearly decelerated and stopped, the pedestrian would certainly have continued crossing the intersection without stopping. Thus, the series of continuous actions of the pedestrian during the incident period fully demonstrated that the pedestrian was "crossing the crosswalk." Third, the interaction between motor vehicles and pedestrians crossing a road intersection without traffic lights is a dynamic process; neither party can accurately predict in advance whether the other will stop and yield. Therefore, the stronger party, the motor vehicle, should proactively stop and yield when encountering a pedestrian crossing the crosswalk, and should not use its strength to force the pedestrian to stop and yield, unless the pedestrian clearly signals the motor vehicle to pass first. This is not only a clear legal requirement but also an inherent demand of modern civilized society to ensure the safe passage of pedestrians as the weaker party, reduce traffic accidents, and protect life safety. In summary, Bei Huifeng drove a motor vehicle approaching a crosswalk when a pedestrian was crossing, and failed to stop to yield, violating Article 47 of the Road Traffic Safety Law of the PRC. The Haining Traffic Police Brigade, based on Bei Huifeng's illegal facts and in accordance with legal procedures, imposed a corresponding administrative penalty within the statutory scope. The facts were clear, the procedure was lawful, and the penalty was appropriate.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Fan Gangjian, Zhang Bocheng, Zhang Hong)

Guiding Case No. 91

Sha Mingbao et al. v. Huashan District People's Government of Ma'anshan City — administrative compensation for forced demolition of a house

(Deliberated and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on November 15, 2017)

Keywords: administrative / administrative compensation / forced demolition / burden of proof / reasonable market value

Ruling Gist

In an administrative compensation case arising from forced demolition of a house, where the plaintiff has provided preliminary evidence, but due to the actions of the administrative agency, the plaintiff is unable to prove the loss of items inside the house, and the administrative agency also fails to prove the loss of items inside the house due to failure to carry out property registration, notarization, or other measures, the people's court shall support the plaintiff's compensation claim for items inside the house that do not exceed market value and conform to common sense of daily life.

Related Legal Provisions

Article 38, Paragraph 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC

Basic Facts

On December 5, 2011, the People's Government of Anhui Province issued Document Wan Zheng Di [2011] No. 769, "Reply on the 35th Batch of Urban Construction Land in 2011 in Ma'anshan City," approving the expropriation of 10.04 hectares of collective construction land for agriculture within the Huoli Subdistrict of Huashan District, Ma'anshan City, for urban construction. On December 23, 2011, the Ma'anshan City People's Government issued Document No. 37 of 2011, "Notice of the Ma'anshan City People's Government on the Plan for Land Expropriation," publishing the contents of the Anhui Provincial People's Government's reply, stating that the expropriation plan would be implemented by the Huashan District People's Government. The house located at B11-3, Fengshou Village, Fengshou Farmers' Group, Huoli Town, Huashan District, under the name of Su Yuehua, fell within the scope of this expropriation. Su Yuehua passed away on September 13, 2011, and had disposed of the house to the four plaintiffs before her death. Plaintiff Gu Hongying is Su Yuehua's daughter; plaintiffs Sha Mingbao, Sha Minghu, and Sha Mingli are Su Yuehua's grandchildren. During the expropriation process, the expropriation authority prepared the "Compensation Table for Expropriation Costs of National Construction Land in Ma'anshan City" and the "Recordation Table for Monetized Housing Resettlement (Property Rights Exchange) for Expropriation in Ma'anshan City," registering and compensating for Su Yuehua's house and aboveground attachments. The husband of plaintiff Gu Hongying received the resettlement compensation. In early 2012, the defendant organized authorities to demolish Su Yuehua's house and aboveground attachments. Plaintiffs Sha Mingbao and three others believed that the Huashan District People's Government of Ma'anshan City illegally demolished the above house, infringing on their lawful property rights, and thus filed a lawsuit, requesting the people's court to order the Huashan District People's Government of Ma'anshan City to compensate for house loss, decoration loss, and rent loss totaling RMB 2,827,680; and for loss of items inside the house totaling RMB 100,000, mainly including clothing, furniture, household appliances, mobile phones, etc., amounting to RMB 50,000; and a solid wood carved bed valued at RMB 50,000.

The Ma'anshan Intermediate People's Court rendered a judgment dismissing the compensation claims of the four plaintiffs, Sha Mingbao et al. Sha Mingbao et al. disagreed and appealed, arguing: 1. In early 2012, when the Huashan District People's Government of Ma'anshan City expropriated the collective agricultural land in question, it did not solicit public opinions, and the appellants did not know on what standard compensation was based; 2. The behavior of the Huashan District People's Government of Ma'anshan City in demolishing the appellants' house on August 1, 2012, was illegal. No agreement was reached beforehand, no notice of demolition was given, and the property inside the house was not moved out or inventoried. The resulting property losses should be borne by the Huashan District People's Government of Ma'anshan City for the burden of proof; 3. On August 27, 2012, the father of appellants Sha Mingbao, Sha Minghu, and Sha Mingli, Sha Kaijin, signed the compensation table under duress. However, his father Sha Kaijin had no rights to the house, and the compensation table was signed after the house was demolished. Therefore, the appellants requested the court of second instance to revoke the first instance judgment and support their compensation claims.

The Huashan District People's Government of Ma'anshan City did not submit a written defense.

Judgment

The Ma'anshan Intermediate People's Court rendered administrative compensation judgment (2015) Ma Xing Pei Chu Zi No. 00004 on July 20, 2015: Dismissed the compensation claims of Sha Mingbao et al. After the judgment was pronounced, Sha Mingbao et al. appealed. The Anhui High People's Court rendered administrative compensation judgment (2015) Wan Xing Pei Zhong Zi No. 00011 on November 24, 2015: Set aside the administrative compensation judgment (2015) Ma Xing Pei Chu Zi No. 00004 of the Ma'anshan Intermediate People's Court; ordered the Huashan District People's Government of Ma'anshan City to compensate the appellants Sha Mingbao et al. for loss of items inside the house in the amount of RMB 80,000.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held: According to Article 45 of the Regulations on the Implementation of the Land Administration Law of the PRC, if the land administration authority orders the surrender of land within a specified period, and the person whose land is expropriated refuses to surrender, the authority shall apply to the people's court for compulsory enforcement. The evidence provided by the Huashan District People's Government of Ma'anshan City could not prove that the plaintiffs voluntarily surrendered the house on the expropriated land. The defendant organized and implemented the demolition of the house of Sha Mingbao et al. without the land administration authority making an order to surrender the land or applying to the people's court for compulsory enforcement, and the act was illegal. Regarding the loss of items inside the demolished house, according to Article 38, Paragraph 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, in cases of administrative compensation or indemnity, the plaintiff shall provide evidence of the damage caused by the administrative act. If the plaintiff is unable to provide evidence due to the defendant's reasons, the burden of proof shall be borne by the defendant. When the Huashan District People's Government of Ma'anshan City organized the demolition of the appellants' house, it did not lawfully register and preserve the items inside the house, nor did it prepare an inventory of items for the appellants to sign and confirm, thereby rendering the appellants unable to prove the damage to items. Therefore, whether such losses existed and the specific loss situation should be borne by the Huashan District People's Government of Ma'anshan City as a matter of law. The appellants claimed RMB 50,000 for items inside the house, including clothing, furniture, household appliances, mobile phones, etc., which were all daily necessities and consistent with the actual circumstances of an ordinary household. The appellee also did not provide evidence that these items did not exist. Therefore, the types, quantities, and values of the items claimed by the appellants should be affirmed. The appellants claimed that the solid wood carved bed was valued at RMB 50,000, which exceeded the normal market price range, and they could not confirm the material, production date, or differences from ordinary solid wood carved beds. The court did not support this claim. However, considering the principle of maximizing protection of the infringed party's lawful rights and interests, and taking into account the current market price of ordinary solid wood carved beds, applying the "prefer the higher rather than the lower" principle, the court comprehensively determined the value of the solid wood carved bed at RMB 30,000. In summary, the court rendered the above judgment.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Wang Xinlin, Song Xin, Ruan Xiufang)

Guiding Case No. 92

Laizhou Jinhai Seed Industry Co., Ltd. v. Zhangye Fukai Agricultural Science and Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of new plant variety rights

(Deliberated and adopted by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on November 15, 2017)

Keywords: civil / infringement of new plant variety rights / maize variety identification / DNA fingerprint detection / similar variety / burden of proof

Ruling Gist

According to the detection and judgment standards of the agricultural industry standard of the PRC "Maize Variety Identification DNA Fingerprinting Method" NY/T1432-2007, if the number of differential loci between varieties is equal to 1, the varieties are deemed similar; if the number of differential loci is 2 or more, the varieties are deemed different. A number of differential loci equal to 1 is insufficient to determine that they are not the same variety. For differential loci of less than 2, other factors shall be considered comprehensively to determine whether they are different varieties, such as expanding the detection loci for additional testing, or submitting tested samples for determination. The burden of proof shall be borne by the alleged infringing party.

Related Legal Provisions

Article 16, Article 17 of the Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties of the PRC

Basic Facts

On January 1, 2003, upon approval by the Ministry of Agriculture, "Jinhai No. 5" was granted a new plant variety right of the PRC, with variety number CNA20010074.2, and the variety right holder was Laizhou Jinhai Crop Research Institute Co., Ltd. On January 8, 2010, the variety right holder authorized Laizhou Jinhai Seed Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Jinhai Seed Industry Company") with the exclusive right to produce and market the maize hybrid "Jinhai No. 5," and authorized Jinhai Seed Industry Company to independently initiate lawsuits in its own name against infringements of unauthorized production and sale of the variety. In 2011, Zhangye Fukai Agricultural Science and Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Fukai Company") conducted maize seed production in Group 8 and Group 11, Gucheng Village, Shajing Town, Ganzhou District, Zhangye City. Jinhai Seed Industry Company filed a lawsuit with the Zhangye Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter "Zhangye Intermediate Court") on the grounds that Fukai Company's seed production infringed its new plant variety right for "Jinhai No. 5" maize. After acceptance, based on Jinhai Seed Industry Company's application, on September 13, 2011, the Zhangye Intermediate Court conducted evidence preservation at the live maize plants in Group 8 and Group 11, Gucheng Village, Shajing Town, by randomly extracting maize ears from the live plants and sealing them on site. The court commissioned the Maize Seed Detection Center of Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences to conduct a comparative identification between the extracted samples and the standard sample of "Jinhai No. 5" preserved at the Plant Variety Protection Office of the Ministry of Agriculture. The detection report issued by the center concluded "no significant difference."

The Zhangye Intermediate Court ruled that infringement was established and ordered Fukai Company to bear liability for infringement. Fukai Company disagreed and appealed to the Gansu High People's Court (hereinafter "Gansu High Court"). After trial, the Gansu High Court found that the original judgment had unclear facts and issued a ruling to remand the case to the Zhangye Intermediate Court for retrial.

After the case was remanded for retrial, the Zhangye Intermediate People's Court sent a letter to the Maize Seed Testing Center of the Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences, requesting a supplementary appraisal or explanation of the testing report numbered "JA2011-098-006," which concluded "no significant difference." The Center replied: "When comparing the tested sample with the control sample of Jinhai No. 5, a protected variety under the Ministry of Agriculture, there was a difference at only 1 locus out of 40 loci. Based on the industry standard, it is determined to be similar, and the conclusion is that there is no significant difference between the tested sample and the control sample. This conclusion should be interpreted as follows: Under the DNA fingerprint testing standard, a difference of at least two loci is taken as a sufficient condition for determining that two samples are different. Where the number of differential loci is less than two, it indicates that the conditions for determining that the two samples are different under that standard are not sufficient, and therefore, a conclusion that the tested sample is different from the control sample cannot be reached." Upon cross-examination, Jinhai Seed Industry Company did not object to the testing report. Fukai Company argued that the testing report indicated the number of differential loci was "1," which showed that the defendant had not infringed, and thus the testing report could not be admitted as evidence in this case.

Judgment

The Zhangye Intermediate People's Court rendered civil judgment (2012) Zhang Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 28, ordering: The claim of Laizhou Jinhai Seed Industry Co., Ltd. is dismissed. Laizhou Jinhai Seed Industry Co., Ltd. refused to accept the judgment and filed an appeal. The Gansu High People's Court rendered civil judgment (2013) Gan Min San Zhong Zi No. 63 on September 17, 2014: 1. The civil judgment (2012) Zhang Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 28 of the Zhangye Intermediate People's Court is set aside. 2. Zhangye Fukai Agricultural Science and Technology Co., Ltd. shall immediately cease the act of infringing the new plant variety right of Laizhou Jinhai Seed Industry Co., Ltd., and compensate Laizhou Jinhai Seed Industry Co., Ltd. for economic losses in the amount of RMB 500,000.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that: Without the permission of the variety rights holder, producing or selling the propagating material of an authorized variety for commercial purposes constitutes an act of infringing the new plant variety right. The core issue in determining whether the propagating material of a new plant variety produced or sold by an actor is the propagating material of an authorized variety lies in whether the characteristics and traits of the new plant variety cultivated using that propagating material are identical to the characteristics and traits of the authorized variety. In this case, upon commission by the people's court, the appraisal opinion issued by the Maize Seed Testing Center of the Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences indicated that the tested sample and the authorized sample showed "no significant difference," but at 40 loci compared in the DNA fingerprint test, there was a difference at one locus. According to the provisions of the agricultural industry standard of the People's Republic of China "Maize Variety Identification DNA Fingerprinting Method NY/T1432-2007 Testing and Judgment Standard": When the number of differential loci between varieties equals 1, they are determined to be similar varieties; when the number of differential loci between varieties is greater than or equal to 2, they are determined to be different varieties. Under the DNA fingerprint testing standard, a difference of at least two loci is taken as the standard for determining whether two varieties are different. When the number of differential loci between varieties equals 1, it is insufficient to conclude that they are not the same variety. There is no direct correspondence between loci in DNA testing and DUS testing. When the number of differential loci is less than two, a determination should be made by considering other factors, such as expanding the number of tested loci for additional testing or submitting certified samples for testing. At this point, the burden of proof should be borne by the party alleged to have infringed. Since the method on which the grant of a new plant variety right is based is DUS testing, not laboratory DNA fingerprint identification, if Zhangye Fukai Agricultural Science and Technology Co., Ltd. submitted contrary evidence proving through DUS testing that the characteristics and traits of the alleged infringing propagating material are not identical to the characteristics and traits of the authorized variety, then the aforementioned conclusion could be overturned. Based on the facts found, after explanation by the court, the appellee Fukai Company still failed to provide contrary evidence and also did not have the conditions for DUS testing. Therefore, pursuant to Article 2, Paragraph 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Infringement of New Plant Variety Rights, which provides: "Without the permission of the variety rights holder, producing or selling the propagating material of an authorized variety for commercial purposes, or repeatedly using the propagating material of an authorized variety for commercial purposes in the production of the propagating material of another variety, the people's court shall determine that it constitutes infringement of the new plant variety right," it should be determined that Fukai Company's act constitutes infringement of the new plant variety right.

Regarding the issue of liability for infringement. Pursuant to Article 6 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Infringement of New Plant Variety Rights, Fukai Company shall bear civil liability for ceasing the infringement and compensating for losses. Since the infringement in this case occurred three years ago, neither party was able to provide sufficient evidence regarding the losses suffered by the infringed party due to the infringement or the profits gained by the infringer due to the infringement. The court found that the acreage planted with the infringing variety was 1,000 mu. Taking into comprehensive consideration factors such as the time, nature, and circumstances of the infringement, the court determined discretionary compensation of RMB 500,000 and ordered the cessation of the infringing act.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Kang Tianxiang, Dou Guilan, Li Xueliang)
